label: letter u input at original position >= 5
explanation: Fires when the input token is u during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 5 (only reachable for L >= 6). Every such step activates (precision 1.0). Never fires on u at positions 0-4, on other tokens, at <DEL>, or in the copy phase (including when u is the output or the copied-back input). Magnitude grows with position: in the examples, u at t=5 sits around 0.15-0.2 of max, t=6 around 0.46-0.49, and t=7-8 up to about 1.0. It is also larger when u is the last original token right before <DEL>; the top examples are all u at t=8 in L=9 sequences. Preceding tokens and first token have no effect.

issues: One magnitude claim is overstated. The explanation says activation is larger when u is the last original token right before <DEL>. When position is held fixed, the data does not show this. On test, u at t=7 with L=8 (u is last) has mass recall 0.157 over 2692 steps. u at t=7 with L=9 (u is not last) has 0.164 over 2815 steps, nearly the same per step. u at t=5 with L=6 versus L=9 is also equal per step (0.041/2794 vs 0.040/2711). The top examples are all u at t=8 only because t=8 can only be the last token when L<=9, so 'last token' and 't=8' are confounded. Magnitude depends on absolute position t, not on whether u is the final token.

The misses follow a pattern but are negligible: all 165 test misses are tiny activations (0.01-0.03 of max) on non-u tokens at step 8, the last original token of L=9 sequences. They carry 0.0% of the mass, so the predicate does not need to change.

Everything else checks out. There are 0 false positives on test. The feature never fires at t<=4, has 3 dev hits at the delimiter / t=9 (counted in the 0.6% of misses, not literally zero), and has 0 copy-phase hits. Preceding tokens and the first token do not matter (flat lift). Mean magnitude per step rises with t (t=5 lowest, t=8 highest).
